text: BFS vs DFS: Why Infinite Depth Changes Completeness Key statement: (what “complete” means):A search method is complete if it is guaranteed to find a solution whenever a solution exists at some finite depth. @ Assume finite branching factor (b < co) and left-to-right expansion. 2 infinite branch @ The tree may have unlimited depth (it can go on forever)_ goal at finite depth @ Suppose a goal exists at some finite depth d. Q @ Q What happenS? keeps going . .. @ BFS: explores levels 0,1,2,... so it will reach depth d and find the goal Q = complete. Takeaway: BFS can't “miss” a finite-depth goal; DFS @ DFS: may follow one infinite branch forever and can. never backtrack to the goal branch = not complete (in infinite-depth spaces).
